title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: One quick fix, two different places
summary: The Suppress quick fix on an unused declaration wrote its annotation above the doc comment in one case and under it in the other. It now writes it on the declaration.

highlights.title: Suppress Lands On The Declaration
highlights.description: An annotation written above a KDoc pushes that comment inside the declaration, where it documents nothing. The Suppress quick fix now writes it on the declaration's own line, under the doc comment, like the four other unused code families.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: The Suppress quick fix on an unused declaration put `@Suppress("unused")` above the declaration's doc comment whenever a removal was available, and on the declaration itself whenever the removal was withheld. One shape, two answers. An annotation above a KDoc pushes that comment inside the declaration, where it is no longer the doc comment of anything, so the annotation now lands on the declaration's own line in both cases.

That is where the four other unused code families have always put it: unused symbols, unused members, and write only variables twice. This one reused the first line of the cut, which is a different question: a cut has to swallow the doc comment, an annotation has to sit under it.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: The removal itself did not move. It still takes the doc comment away with the declaration, and the check over the reference project confirms it: 93 cuts across 5110 sources, every invariant at zero.
